 Russia claims it protects vulnerable children from war zones, but critics argue that many deported children have had their identities changed and been subjected to abuse by Russian families. 

 [RSnake: It’s a nice gesture, but it’s unlikely to have any effect at all, sadly.] 

Source: https://euromaidanpress.com/?p=355193 

 

 China has unveiled a vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) drone powered by a jet engine, capable of operating from various naval vessels, which could significantly extend the operational reach of the Chinese navy. This development represents a potential shift in maritime warfare tactics and could enhance China's military capabilities in regional conflicts, particularly concerning Taiwan and the South China Sea. 

 China's new VTOL drone can turn any ship into a strike platform, enhancing its naval capabilities. 

 The drone could influence regional security dynamics, especially in potential conflicts involving Taiwan. 

 [RSnake: I haven’t seen a video of the VTOL yet, just some grainy pics of its sleek airframe. But the article is correct that if such a thing exists, it would greatly increase the practical utility of vessels that have a large enough deck to allow for the airframes to take off and land.] 

Source: https://www.eurasiantimes.com/?p=250323 

 

 China is pursuing an aggressive total war strategy against the US that leverages next-generation weapons and irregular warfare tools, including bioweapons, nanoweapons, and psychological manipulation. 

 The CCP has been pursuing an aggressive, multifaceted total war against the US that leverages next-generation weapons, including synthetic narcotics, bioweapons, psychological manipulation, and irregular warfare tools. 

 The CCP's total war strategy involves convergent WMD programs, academic subversion, and non-kinetic shifts, mainly through the exploitation of Western openness in academia, technology, and media to erode US advantages without direct kinetic conflict. 

 [RSnake: And so many other things. Unrestricted Warfare is an old book, but a pretty good idea of how the generals over in the CCP are thinking about us and their capabilities.] 

Source: https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/chinas-assassins-mace-irregular-warfare-campaign-may-render-trumps-golden-dome-useless 

 

 Representative Delia Ramirez is facing criticism for her response to a question about what it means to be an American, with some arguing that she has conditional loyalty to Guatemala rather than the US. The question was part of a discussion on colonialism and reparations. Congresswoman Ramirez stated that being an American means recognizing the good and bad of the country's formation and acknowledging past evils. 

 Representative Delia Ramirez is facing criticism for her response to a question about what it means to be an American. 

 Some argue that she has a conditional loyalty to Guatemala, rather than the US, while others contend that she has no right to claim citizenship in the first place. 

 The conversation surrounding colonialism and reparations highlights deeper issues of identity and loyalty among immigrants and citizens. 

 [RSnake: I am a little wary of throwing the baby out with the bathwater here. I do think multiculturalism has a huge impact on everything, from food to dance, to ideas, to language, to decor, and all kinds of things. If we get totally homogeneous, we’ll lose some of that. While it’s not great to want our country to be like other countries, it’s also not sensible to think we don’t have things to learn from other national experiments. And yes, the US has made mistakes that are worthy of note.] 

Source: https://www.dailywire.com/news/what-is-an-american-not-delia-ramirez 

 

 Over 20 Baha'i members in Iran have had their homes, assets, and vehicles confiscated under Article 49 of the constitution, which allows authorities to confiscate wealth obtained through illegal means without evidence or transparency. The seizures are part of a long-running pattern of property seizures against Baha'is since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. Baha'i families face blocked bank accounts, frozen business transaction,s and restrictions on selling or transferring property. 

 Baha'i community in Iran has faced systematic repression over the past five years, including at least 284 arrests and 1,495 years in combined prison sentences. 

 Baha'is account for an average of 72% of all recorded violations against religious minorities in Iran over the past three years. 

 [RSnake: Not entirely surprising that Iran is running low on cash and needs to steal from its people.] 

Source: https://www.iranintl.com/en/202508159303 

 

 Jimmy Lai, a pro-democracy media tycoon in Hong Kong, is currently undergoing a national security trial that has been postponed due to health issues and weather conditions. Lai, detained since December 2020, faces life imprisonment if convicted, with international attention focused on his case amid ongoing concerns about the suppression of dissent in Hong Kong under a new security law implemented by Beijing. 

 Jimmy Lai is on trial for colluding with foreign forces under China's national security law. 

 His case highlights the broader implications for political dissent and legal rights in Hong Kong. 

 [RSnake: Make no mistake, China is a communist authoritarian nightmare for anyone who is a free thinker.] 

Source: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cgm2z7497yko?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss 

 

 The United States is developing a $175 billion multi-layered missile defense system called Golden Dome, which aims to protect the US homeland from ballistic, hypersonic, and cruise missiles, as well as other advanced aerial threats. 

 The Golden Dome system will have four layers: one space-based and three land-based layers, including a constellation of satellites for missile warning, tracking, and interception, focusing on boost-phase intercepts. 

 The system aims to integrate existing missile defense technologies with new innovations, creating a multi-layered defense architecture to intercept threats at various stages of flight, including the boost phase, midcourse, and terminal phases. 

 [RSnake: Now’s the time. It’s not like countries aren’t looking at what happened in Iran and Yemen against Israel and thinking that ballistic missiles and missile defense are a wise investment.] 

Source: https://www.eurasiantimes.com/?p=250202 

 

 Tuvalu, a Pacific island nation, faces imminent relocation of its population due to rising sea levels that threaten its habitability by mid-century. With sea levels around the islands increasing by 15 centimeters over the past 30 years, Tuvalu is considering becoming the first fully digital nation to preserve its culture and sovereignty as it confronts severe infrastructure, freshwater, and economic challenges. 

 Tuvalu could become the first country to relocate its entire population due to climate change. 

 Rising sea levels threaten the nation's infrastructure, freshwater supply, and economy. 

 Tuvalu plans to create a digital replica of its nation to protect cultural landmarks and sovereignty. 

 [RSnake: Without giving you my opinion on sea rise changes, here is the Wikipedia article on it . That said, do your homework. Either way, it feels like they should get the Saudis to help because they are spectacular at creating artificial land out of the sea floor. China too… with strings attached.] 

Source: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/rest-of-world/for-the-first-time-in-history-an-entire-country-might-move-its-whole-population-the-reason-will-shock-you/articleshow/123288803.cms 

 

 Federal authorities have arrested over 100 people in Washington, D.C., since last Thursday as part of President Trump's violent crime crackdown, involving hundreds of National Guard troops and multiple federal agencies. 

 The US government has deployed the National Guard and federalized local police to combat violent crime in Washington, D.C. 

 [RSnake: And a lot of people started going out to enjoy restaurants as well. So clearly there is a problem that the previous administration ignored or worse, and therefore tacitly encouraged.] 

Source: https://www.dailywire.com/news/d-c-will-be-safe-again-feds-kick-off-trumps-violent-crime-crackdown-with-over-100-arrests 

 

 NASA is transitioning from building its own relay orbiters and spacecraft to buying connectivity as a service for Mars missions, with major contenders pitching ways to keep data pipes online. 

 NASA aims to create an interoperable marketplace where it can be one of many customers, rather than the owner-operator. 

 Several companies, including Netflix, ElevenLabs, Wayve, and Sequoia Capital, are pitching solutions for a 'lunar trunkline' between the moon and Earth and end-to-end Mars communications. 

 [RSnake: Now that SpaceX and competitors are finally in the market, this is much more viable than it used to be. This is really where the government is useful, get the moonshot up and running, but then let private industry take it from there.] 

Source: https://techcrunch.com/?p=3036664 

 

 The Air Force has implemented a new policy that mandates the automatic discharge of transgender troops diagnosed with gender dysphoria, removing their ability to appeal through military separation boards. Legal experts and advocacy groups are concerned that this policy undermines impartial evaluation processes in the military and may set a precedent for other military branches to follow. 

 The Air Force now requires mandatory separation of airmen with gender dysphoria, eliminating their chance for defense. 

 This policy change could influence separation processes across other military branches. 

 [RSnake: Wow. Interesting. I wonder if this will get re-classified in the DSM-5 as a paraphilia. I’m not holding my breath.] 

Source: https://www.military.com/daily-news/2025/08/16/new-air-force-policy-denies-transgender-troops-hearings-theyre-discharged.html 

 

 Haiti is facing a severe political and security crisis marked by the expansion of gang influence since the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse in 2021. The newly appointed interim leader, Laurent Saint-Cyr, is tasked with navigating this turmoil, as more than 1.3 million people have been displaced and the country struggles with acute food insecurity. International efforts to stabilize the situation continue, including a potential $1.4 billion aid initiative from the Organization of American States. 

 Laurent Saint-Cyr has been inaugurated as Haiti's new interim leader amid ongoing gang violence and political instability. 

 Over 1.3 million Haitians are internally displaced due to the deteriorating security situation. 

 [RSnake: It’s a real shame, and shows the difference in governments between it and the Dominican Republic, which occupy the same island, and how much policy matters.] 

Source: https://foreignpolicy.com/?p=1203325 

 Cybersecurity 

 Accenture acquires CyberCX to expand cybersecurity capabilities in the Asia Pacific, bolstering its position in the region and enhancing its ability to build business resilience and protect critical infrastructure. 

 Accenture will acquire CyberCX's approximately 1,400 skilled cybersecurity professionals and AI-powered security platforms. 

 The acquisition represents Accenture’s largest cybersecurity acquisition to date and will further expand Accenture’s leading position in the Asia Pacific region. 

 [RSnake: More investments in AI… but, interestingly, Accenture wants to be investing in that region at the moment, all things considered.] 

Source: https://thereadable.co/accenture-to-acquire-cybercx-expanding-cybersecurity-capabilities-in-asia-pacific/ 

 

 ICE inadvertently exposed details of a manhunt in real-time by adding a random person to a group chat, revealing data from DMV and license plate readers. 

 ICE used DMV and license plate reader data to find a target, and an unredacted ICE worksheet was shared in the group chat. 

 The incident is a significant data breach and operational security failure for ICE. 

 [RSnake: Whoops. This is why I don’t like the idea of government employees using civilian apps or even civilian phones while on duty. Just too easy to make mistakes or get compromised.] 

Source: https://www.404media.co/ice-adds-random-person-to-group-chat-exposes-details-of-manhunt-in-real-time/ 

 

 Fortinet has identified a critical remote command execution vulnerability in its FortiSIEM products, with exploit code already available in the wild. Organizations using affected versions of FortiSIEM are urged to apply security updates immediately, as the flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute commands. The vulnerability, designated CVE-2025-25256, has a high CVSS rating of 9.8, indicating severe risk for various sectors, including government and healthcare. 

 Fortinet's FortiSIEM has a critical flaw allowing unauthorized command execution. 

 Exploit code for this flaw exists in the wild, necessitating immediate action from organizations. 

 [RSnake: You know, other than the year in the CVE, you couldn’t tell what year this report came from. Now, is anyone still using Internet-exposed Fortinet devices at this point?] 

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/fortinet-warns-of-fortisiem-pre-auth-rce-flaw-with-exploit-in-the-wild/ 

 

 Cisco has announced a critical remote code execution vulnerability in its Secure Firewall Management Center software, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands due to improper input handling during the authentication process. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2025-20265, has a severity score of 10 out of 10, prompting Cisco to release patches and recommend alternative authentication methods for affected users. Additionally, Cisco addressed multiple other high-severity flaws across its product range. 

 Cisco disclosed a critical RCE vulnerability in its Secure Firewall Management Center. 

 The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote command execution due to improper input handling. 

 Cisco recommends immediate patching or alternative authentication methods for affected users. 

 [RSnake: Cisco is better than Fortinet, but really, these issues have got to start getting dealt with much earlier, and before they are used in the wild.] 

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisco-warns-of-max-severity-flaw-in-firewall-management-center/ 

 

 Recent studies reveal that cybercriminal groups are exploiting brokerage services by using sophisticated phishing kits to manipulate stock prices through a new scheme called 'ramp and dump.' These fraudsters utilize multiple compromised accounts to buy large volumes of targeted stocks, inflating their prices before selling, resulting in substantial losses for unsuspecting investors. This activity highlights vulnerabilities in the multi-factor authentication processes of brokerage platforms, which are increasingly being targeted due to their reduced security amid evolving phishing tactics. 

 Cybercriminals are shifting focus to manipulating stock prices through compromised brokerage accounts. 

 The new 'ramp and dump' scheme exploits vulnerabilities in multi-factor authentication systems of brokerage firms. 

 [RSnake: Impressive. This typically requires a substantial number of shares to produce any noticeable market movement. However, it is a nice way to conceal the real trades because they are often overshadowed by the noise of many buyers and sellers in a market. I know small traders who have tried something similar with tons of brokerage accounts and penny stocks.] 

Source: https://krebsonsecurity.com/?p=71895 

 

 The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) is increasingly being targeted by cyberattacks, leading to potential threats to patient health and data security. A new framework for a hierarchical intrusion detection system (IDS) has been proposed to effectively detect zero-day attacks within these networks, with experimental results showing high accuracy in identifying threats. This advancement aims to enhance security in resource-constrained environments where traditional IDS solutions have limitations. 

 A hierarchical IDS framework is designed to detect zero-day attacks in Internet of Medical Things networks. 

 The proposed solution achieves a detection accuracy of 99.77% and an F1-score of 97.8%, demonstrating its high applicability in IoMT environments. 

 [RSnake: It does make sense as a cyber ransom - do what I say or I’ll kill a bunch of your company’s customers. of… imagine that press release.] 

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10346 

 

 Wyoming and South Dakota are expanding age verification laws, applying them to a broader range of websites beyond just porn sites. 

 Age verification laws in Wyoming and South Dakota do not include the 33.3% provision that most other states have adopted, potentially requiring more websites to implement age verification measures. 

 The laws could create civil and criminal liability for social media platforms, retailers, streaming services, and other platforms hosting adult content or material deemed harmful to minors without adequate age verification measures in place. 

 [RSnake: I don’t see how this works unless everyone does it all at once. If even one corner of the Internet doesn’t care and doesn’t limit access, all porn will head there, and so will the people who want to see it.] 

Source: https://www.404media.co/wyoming-and-south-dakota-age-verification-laws/ 

 

 AI chatbots are being used for therapy and mental health support, but experts say they can be dangerous due to privacy concerns and the lack of regulation. 

 The American Psychological Association (APA) has expressed concern about AI chatbot companies using their claims to pass themselves off as trained mental health providers. 

 Chatbots have no legal obligation to protect user information, making them vulnerable to data breaches and potential harm to vulnerable individuals. 

 [RSnake: Yep, these are not licensed, hallucinate, give bad advice, and disobey HIPAA.] 

Source: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/why-ai-therapy-can-be-so-dangerous/ 

 Technology 

 OpenAI staffers plan to sell $6 billion in stock to SoftBank and other investors, valuing the company at $300 billion, as the AI industry experiences a high-stakes talent war. 

 OpenAI employees can sell shares worth $500 billion, making it the world's most valuable startup. 

 The sale comes after OpenAI secured $8.3 billion from investors and expects revenue to triple this year to $12.7 billion. 

 [RSnake: Weirdest nonprofit ever.] 

Source: https://fortune.com/2025/08/16/openai-staffers-6-billion-secondary-stock-sale-softbank-thrive-capital-dragoneer/ 

 

 Discoveries from the James Webb Telescope are challenging our understanding of the universe, including its expansion rate, galaxy formation, and the nature of dark matter. 

 The James Webb Telescope has made groundbreaking discoveries that contradict our current understanding of the universe, including its expansion rate, galaxy formation, and the nature of dark matter. 

 These findings have sparked a wave of bold new theories, revisions to textbooks, and a renewed debate about fundamental physics and cosmology. 

 [RSnake: The synopsis sucks, but the article goes into a bunch of different things that James Webb has found so far. I saw it before it went into space, so it has a special place in my heart.] 

Source: https://thenextweb.com/news/james-webb-telescope-discoveries-european-tech 

 

 Apple has effectively abandoned its original vision for the iPad, turning it into a full-blown multitasking, window-wrangling computer that can now replace a Mac for many users. 

 Apple has turned the iPad into a full-blown multitasking, window-wrangling computer with iPadOS 26. 

 The new operating system brings features like modern multitasking, windowing, and external display support, making it more like a Mac than ever before. 

 [RSnake: It’s coming this fall, but for those of you who use it, you might find that it is a laptop replacement or certainly reduces the need for a laptop. So, if you prefer a beefy desktop most of the time but want something super portable, you could theoretically use an iPad. I don’t think devs will go this path unless they can VPN back into their main desktop for terminal access.] 

Source: https://www.wired.com/story/apple-finally-destroyed-steve-jobss-vision-of-the-ipad-good/ 

 

 Senator Josh Hawley is launching an investigation into Meta after a leaked internal document suggested that the company's AI chatbots were designed to engage in questionable conversations with children. The senator has requested documentation from Meta regarding their AI content standards and the specific individuals involved in these decisions, amid widespread public disapproval of the findings. 

 Sen. Josh Hawley is investigating Meta's AI policies concerning interactions with children. 

 The investigation follows the leak of a document revealing inappropriate chatbot behaviors sanctioned by Meta's legal team. 

 [RSnake: Oof, also there are questionable chat rooms like “Russian girl” and “Step Mom” and “Granny Cougar”. Gross.] 

Source: https://gizmodo.com/?p=2000643975 

 

 Ukrainian drones were deployed in Russia from hidden civilian-style containers, striking Moscow's fleet of long-range bombers and damaging several. The development of missile launch systems disguised as ordinary vehicles is a trend globally, with countries like China, Iran, North Korea, Russia, and the US involved. This points to a high-threat environment ahead of the 2030s. 

 Drones are being used in Russia from hidden civilian-style containers. 

 This is part of a global trend of developing missile launch systems disguised as ordinary vehicles. 

 [RSnake: Taiwan has a hellfire missile in a truck design that the article pointed to that looks pretty effective and stealthy.] 

 hellfire
 

 Source: https://www.zerohedge.com/military/hellfire-missile-launcher-hidden-inside-civilian-box-truck 

 

 Roblox faces a lawsuit over alleged failure to implement basic safety controls and facilitate the distribution of child sexual abuse material. 

 Roblox has 82 million daily active users, including 20% under the age of 8 and another 20% between 9 and 12, making it vulnerable to predators. 

 The platform allows adults to pose as children and children to bypass age requirements, exposing them to explicit content and potential abuse. 

 [RSnake: If your kids use Robolox, you should probably have a conversation with them about it, not to take or share photos, and if they see anything with nude people in it, to let you know immediately.] 

Source: https://techcrunch.com/?p=3037219 

 Business 

 Matt Stone and Trey Parker, the creators of the television show South Park, have each become billionaires through lucrative deals with Paramount, including a $1.5 billion agreement to stream their show's entire catalog. They have a history of innovative deal-making and a unique creative process that has contributed to their continued success in the entertainment industry. 

 Stone and Parker have signed a $1.5 billion streaming deal with Paramount+. 

 They are known for their unique and controversial brand of humor that continues to resonate with audiences. 

 Their business model leverages back-end ownership of their intellectual property, which has become increasingly rare in the industry. 

 [RSnake: And the latest South Park had more naked depictions of Trump. They do not care. They’re pretty brave, that’s all I can say. I could see a situation where Trump pressures Paramount+ in about 100 ways, and they end up canceling South Park and suing Stone and Parker for damages, indirectly. Or Trump rides the wave of earned media… either way, it’s brave and likely inconsequential for Trump.] 

Source: https://www.readtrung.com/p/south-park-and-the-greatest-tv-contract 

 

 President Trump has taken a commanding role in the semiconductor industry, imposing new fees on exports to China and directly negotiating conditions with tech CEOs, such as the CEO of Nvidia. Interventions have prompted significant changes in the industry's operations and investments, with major companies needing to navigate these demands for U.S. manufacturing and financial contributions. 

 Trump is directly negotiating export licenses and conditions with major technology companies. 

 His involvement has created uncertainty in the semiconductor sector, leading to increased pressure on companies to comply with his demands. 

 [RSnake: This is likely not legal, btw. However, the ones to sue would be companies like Nvidia and Intel, and they would prefer to make 85% than lose 100%. Also, in related news, there are still those rumors about backdoors in Nvidia chips en route to China.] 

Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/13/technology/trump-chips-nvidia-intel.html 

 

 As AI agents become increasingly prevalent in digital commerce, brands must adapt to a new landscape where algorithms take the lead in making purchasing decisions. Brands that fail to optimize for machine experience risk falling behind, while those that succeed will reap significant rewards. The agent economy is no longer speculative; it is now investable, and brands must prioritize data-driven marketing strategies to stay relevant. 

 Brands must operationalize loyalty across two separate fronts: emotional and algorithmic. 

 Marketing to machines requires real-time relevance and quantifiable value, rather than charm or creativity. 

 [RSnake: Yep, and brands that block LLMs and don’t have an LLM strategy will subsequently get what they pay for - obscurity.] 

Source: https://www.fastcompany.com/91383862/why-brands-need-to-court-ai-agents 

 

 Yi He, co-founder of Binance and an influential figure in the cryptocurrency industry, has emerged as a central leader following the company's management turmoil. Despite significant challenges, including a historic legal settlement and loss of the original CEO, Binance remains the largest cryptocurrency exchange globally, focusing on compliance and customer service. The cryptocurrency market continues to evolve, with expectations of deeper integration into the traditional financial system in the coming years. 

 Yi He has taken on a more public role at Binance, demonstrating leadership during a challenging period. 

 Binance has maintained its position as the largest cryptocurrency exchange despite regulatory issues and internal changes. 

 The crypto market is expected to further integrate with traditional finance through advancements in blockchain technology. 

 [RSnake: We shall see! I still don’t know where Trump will land with this case, even if he is pro crypto. I think Trump would need to have some deal made with him before he came out in support. Why else would he stick his neck out?] 

Source: https://fortune.com/crypto/2025/08/13/binance-yi-he/ 

 Share this newsletter 

 Got a helpful tip? Looking to chat with me? Click here . 

 Check out the RSnake Show as well. 

 Full Disclosure: None of this is advice. This newsletter is strictly educational and my opinions. Please exercise caution, conduct your research, and consult a professional before taking any action based on the information presented here.

subject: RSnake Report 20250810
subtitle: Texas Dems to be arrested, China's entrepreneurs failing, etc
body_text:
What's In the News

 Geopolitics 

 Cybersecurity 

 Technology 

 Business 

 Hello, and thanks for reading! I’m freshly back from Blackhat, which, for those of you not in security, is one of the largest security conferences in the world. It was a lot of handshaking and answering questions about the new company we are starting. Overall, a great week, and I am more than a little exhausted from the travel. Opportunity abounds at that conference in the security industry writ large. 

 In Russia/Ukraine News, another railway traction electrical substation in Rostov has been obliterated, disrupting Russian logistics. The attack on the Tatsinskaya railway station saw Russian sources claiming to have shot down dozens of UAVs , though the veracity of these claims remains suspect as Ukraine's drone operations continue to evolve. 

 “Railway traction electrical substation destroyed in Rostov”
 

 Ukrainian forces have increasingly targeted Russian fuel trains , suggesting a sophisticated intelligence operation that allows them to track and strike these critical supply lines, likely headed to the front, but also to key logistics and shipping hubs. One such example was a drone attack on an oil depot in Adler, Sochi , and a significant strike on the Afipsky oil refinery in the Krasnodar region. The latter processes about 7 million tons of oil annually, and the drone strike caused a substantial fire and reportedly destroyed the primary crude oil pumping terminal. But there have been a number of such attacks that switch targets so that the Russian air defenses have to keep moving and guessing where the next wave will originate from. That forces them to stretch their resources thin.

 The ripple effect of these attacks is felt economically, with Ukraine's strategic targeting aiming to weaken Russia's financial backbone.  Tesla is experiencing a used-car collapse due to the company's CEO, Elon Musk's, controversial political actions, leading to a decline in sales and profits, with the Cybertruck being a major symbol of this decline. 

 The average price of a used Tesla has plummeted by 30.35% in the last year, now hovering around $84,027. 

 Used Tesla prices have dropped below the average for the entire US used car market, with the Model S, Model X, and Model Y also experiencing significant declines. 

 [RSnake: It’s a steal if you like his cars. But it’s gotta be giving shareholders heartburn.] 

Source: https://gizmodo.com/?p=2000641133 

 

 Recent U.S. job market data indicates weaker-than-expected hiring, prompting discussions among Federal Reserve officials about the need for potential interest rate cuts. Some officials believe that lower rates could stimulate the economy, while concerns about inflation persist, particularly in light of Trump's tariffs, which may complicate the Fed's ability to manage economic stability. Investors now anticipate that the Fed may need to act quickly to cut rates in response to the latest economic signals. 

 Federal Reserve officials are considering cutting interest rates due to disappointing job market reports. 

 There are concerns regarding inflation levels and the impact of tariffs on the economy. 

 [RSnake: Quite a few of these jobs were government jobs, so it’s not exactly as bad as it looks, but it’s not great. AI is the main culprit in the tech industry.] 

Source: https://fortune.com/2025/08/09/fed-rate-cuts-outlook-michelle-bowman-jobs-report-inflation-tariffs/ 

 

 A new bull market has emerged in the U.S., with the S&P 500 index rising nearly 30% since its April lows. Analysts are optimistic due to easing fears over tariffs and potential strong earnings, although some caution exists regarding possible market volatility in the third quarter. 

 The S&P 500 has surged approximately 30% since April, signaling the end of a bear market. 

 Analysts predict ongoing optimism in the stock market, driven by strong earnings and economic factors. 

 [RSnake: And yet interest rates are stubbornly fixed. Pretty frustrating.] 

Source: https://fortune.com/2025/08/09/new-bull-market-buy-the-dips-stock-outlook-sp500/ 

 Share this newsletter 

 Got a useful tip? Looking to chat with me? Click here . 

 Check out the RSnake Show as well. 

 Full Disclosure: None of this is advice. This newsletter is strictly educational and my opinions. Please be careful, do your own research, and consult a professional before taking action on anything posted here.

subtitle: Peace through Tariffs, Israel annexations, etc
body_text:
What's In the News

 Geopolitics 

 Cybersecurity 

 Technology 

 Business 

 Hello, and thanks for reading! It was a massive week for me. We finally announced a $12.5M seed round led by Ballistic Ventures and Grossman Ventures (our fund) for a new vulnerability management company called Evidence . The idea is to use evidence of loss in decision-making to limit risks to organizations. I will be the CTO of Evidence while still being the Managing Director of Grossman Ventures. It's a huge week, especially as we head into Black Hat in Las Vegas, NV. 

 Evidence
 

 In other news, I have just launched a little toy site where I document funny/dumb things about AI. It's called AI IS DOING GREAT , and basically it's just a super fast and easy to read news collection of idiotic things in AI, so that I have it all documented in one place. It is an homage to web3isdoinggreat.com , but focused on AI and LLMs specifically. If you find stupid things about AI, just message me on X ( @RSnake ) and I'll upload it for you. 

 Okay, on with the week in geopolitical news…! 

 In Russian/Ukrainian news , Ukraine's latest drone offensive went largely unreported. The flight paths of these unmanned aerial vehicles, as traced by Russian sources, show how deeply they can penetrate Russian air defenses and do so largely uncontested. Only a few mentions in Russian media popped up, including some interceptions in Rostov . 

 Drone offensive
 

 Russia did the same, with a huge strike package against Kyiv . There were also a few civilian casualties , which seems par for the course with Moscow’s targeting capabilities, or lack thereof. 

 “Horrible night in Kyiv”
 

 The effectiveness of Ukraine's air defenses is waning, a concerning development as Russian drone swarms penetrate deeper into Ukrainian airspace. With penetration rates escalating from 5% in March to a staggering 15% currently , the urgency for Ukraine to bolster its defenses seems palpable. The country's response involves deploying interceptor UAVs at a cost of $5,000 each, a necessary but expensive countermeasure, considering the alternative. 

 “Ukraine rushes interceptor UAVs costing $5K each”
 

 Russian forces have repurposed old rail systems to maintain their supply lines close to the frontlines. A small railway vehicle, capable of transporting 1,000 kg of essential supplies like water, ammunition, and food over distances up to 50 km, represents a creative solution to logistical challenges. This makeshift solution underscores the desperation and resourcefulness of both sides in a conflict where every advantage counts. 

 “1000 kg of water”
 

 Hackers have reportedly dismantled the entire IT infrastructure of Russia's Aeroflot . This cyber operation, lasting a year, culminated in the destruction of critical systems, including databases, internal mail, and executive communications. With around 7,000 servers wiped and over 20TB of data stolen, the financial toll on Aeroflot is estimated to be in the tens of millions of dollars. The immediate fallout saw Aeroflot canceling over 40 flights , resulting in passenger delays at Sheremetyevo Airport, where stranded passengers faced long lines and confusion. 

 “7,000 servers were wiped and over 20TB of data stolen”
 

 The humanitarian crisis in the Donetsk region continues to escalate, exacerbated by the lack of access to clean water. Russian occupation has left the area without a viable water supply, and with extreme heat compounding the issue, the situation is dire. Water trucks from Russia's Rostov region are attempting to alleviate the shortage, but the challenges are immense. Leaky pipes, destroyed water intakes, and pumping stations hinder the delivery efforts, but the real catastrophe lies in the depletion of the water itself. As reported, flooding of mines in the Donetsk coal basin, a consequence of Russian occupation since 2014, has led to an environmental disaster in terms of potable drinking water. But this also affects the soldiers operating in that region as well, on both sides. Meanwhile we are seeing super janky looking motorcycle trailer systems that move small amounts of water to front line troops. 

 “improvised trailer”
 

 Speaking of motorcycles, the Russian military's logistics have taken a creative turn, with 122mm artillery shells now being transported by motorcycle . The death toll among Russian motor transport due to drone attacks has accelerated, pushing the military to adopt these unconventional, unarmored methods of small arms and ordinance transportation. 

 “122mm artillery shells”
 

 Ukrainian drones have struck a significant blow against Russian logistics, destroying a military fuel train at a rail hub in Salsk, Rostov region. As was the Novokuybyshevsk oil refinery . So attacks on oil are still ongoing, which should keep the pressure up economically and make it increasingly unpopular financially. 

 “ELOU AVT-11”
 

 Almost as if God himself had something to say about this conflict, an 8.7 magnitude earthquake off Russia's far east triggered tsunami warnings and advisories across the region. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Tsunami Warning System depicted the severity of the situation, with red, orange, yellow, and purple zones indicating varying levels of threat. 

 “8.7 earthquake hit off of Russia's far east”
 

 Drone footage captured the aftermath , showing extensive flood damage to coastal areas and the port in Severo-Kurilsk on the Kamchatka Peninsula. It is rumored that this has wreaked havoc on the Russian submarine base in the region. 

 “tsunami flood damage to coastal areas”
 

 The proliferation of drone knowledge from the Ukraine conflict has reached unexpected corners of the world. The violent Mexican "Los Zetas" cartel is reportedly infiltrating its members into Ukrainian foreign volunteer units to gain advanced knowledge of FPV drones. Mexican intelligence has warned the Ukrainian SSU, which is now investigating these claims. Something to look forward to, since these cartels will be fighting US soldiers at some point as they clash on the border regions. If there was any hope that we can limit drone proliferation, I think it’s time to face reality. This is going to come back to hurt US soldiers so we had better start taking asymmetric drone conflict seriously. 

 “Los Zetas”
 

 President Donald Trump has announced the deployment of two nuclear submarines in response to provocative statements and nuclear threats from former Russian President Medvedev. Trump's statement caused the MOEX to plummet more than 100 points in the last week . I have heard numerous reports indicating that even the normal pro-Putin propagandists are wary of a US conflict with Trump as President, even as Trump’s “10-12” ultimatum of peace nears. 

 

 In European News , an unknown drone, believed to be Russian, has sparked an emergency alert in Vilnius, Lithuania, after crossing into the country from Belarus. The Lithuanian Police Force and Armed Forces are conducting a mass search for the drone, urging residents to report any sightings or possible landing sites. While this incident raises concerns about potential Russian aggression, it is crucial to note that this does not necessarily constitute an attack on NATO, necessarily, because it may simply be off course or damaged. But if not, it does put NATO in a strange position. 

 Poland is preparing swarms of sea drones for potential conflict with Russia in the Baltic Sea. The country's special forces are testing ultra-cheap sea drones from US-based HavocAI, capable of carrying a payload of about 136 kg and equipped with solar panels to extend their range. I am curious if the range can be virtually unlimited if it is allowed to recharge during the day. Either way, this means Poland is a real threat to Russian surface fleets, shipping, and ports. 

 “ultra-cheap sea drones from HavocAI”
 

 In South East Asia , the week started out with the fragile peace between Cambodia and Thailand having shattered, with Cambodia breaking the ceasefire and launching attacks on the Thai Army at Chong An Ma, Ta Muen Thom, and Phu Makheua. Cambodian forces are not only clashing but also attempting to advance and seize territory, prompting the Thai Army to prepare for action. The Thai military instructed all units to be fully prepared and enter bunkers, signaling a potential escalation of hostilities in the region. 

 But then… Trump threatened both of them with massive Tariffs , and the hostilities ended just like that. 😆 What a difference a week makes. In Cambodia, there are signs thanking Trump for bringing peace. Crazy story that seems to have concluded. That could have easily spread into a much larger Chinese vs US Conflict, so we are very lucky it concluded that quickly. 😮‍💨 

 U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned Chinese officials that continued purchases of sanctioned Russian oil could lead to significant tariffs , as mandated by legislation in Congress. Chinese officials, asserting their sovereignty, have stated that their oil purchases will be based on internal policies, even if it means facing a 100% tariff. The United States has threatened tariffs of up to 500% on imports of sanctioned Russian oil. We shall see how this plays out, but it’s clear we really want to drive a wedge between Russia and China, further economically isolating both of them in the process. 

 In Middle East News , Prime Minister Netanyahu is reportedly preparing a plan for the full annexation of the Gaza Strip . According to Haaretz, Netanyahu intends to present this plan to the security cabinet, giving Hamas a few days to agree to a ceasefire or face gradual annexation of Palestinian territories. Notably, Netanyahu claims that the Trump administration has already endorsed this plan, which doesn’t come as a shock at all, given that Trump has eyes on the real estate potential of the seaside. Simultaneously, the United Kingdom is threatening to recognize Palestine as a state in September, along with a number of Middle Eastern countries, which could further complicate the already volatile situation in the region. I think this will come down to a race to see if Israel can make its goals happen by September or not. 

 In strangely related news, a growing number of Druze in Syria are expressing a desire to be annexed by Israel . At a demonstration in Sweida, southern Syria, chants of "We want Israel!" were heard. Think about it, this will be a situation where they have already taken over Mount Vernon, they’ll take over Gaza and possibly also Southern Syria all within a few months t’ time. That’s a big shift if it does happen. 

 In North American news , Ghislaine Maxwell, convicted of sex trafficking and a close associate of Jeffrey Epstein, has been granted "limited" immunity by the Department of Justice to answer questions related to her convictions. Maxwell reportedly spoke with Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche for close to nine hours, discussing "maybe 100 different people." Her attorney stated that she "didn't hold anything back" and is seeking a pardon from President Trump in exchange for her testimony. So there may be a lot more information coming from this new testimony. It’s not clear what the limited immunity covers, but I suspect it will limit her from prosecution for whatever testimony involves her being an eyewitness to and facilitating child sex trafficking. Pretty gross. 

 In a shocking incident, Shane Devon Tamura, a 27-year-old from Las Vegas, carried out a deadly shooting in Midtown Manhattan at 345 Park Avenue. Armed with an AR-style rifle and wearing a bullet-resistant vest, Tamura killed five people, including an NYPD officer, and injured six others in the 44-story building housing Blackstone and NFL headquarters. After barricading himself on the 33rd floor, Tamura took his own life. Tamura, who had a concealed firearms permit from Las Vegas and a past as a Canadian football player, left a suicide note alleging that he suffered from CTE , a brain disease linked to head trauma. In the note, he expressed grievances against the NFL, stating, "You can't go against the NFL, they'll squash you." 

 “Shane Devon Tamura”
 

 For those of you who don’t know, I believe strongly that my best friend James Flom killed his girlfriend and himself due to auditory hallucinations he had been experiencing, likely due to CTE. So I am very sensitive to this issue and think it is only one of the greatest failings of modern medicine that there is no way to diagnose it until post-mortem. 

 There was a bit of Blackstone drama when they effectively barricaded their office , showing how quick thinking could serve as a model for emergency response. Some people thought it was stupid and that they should have just been carrying guns to take out the attacker, others, who carry guns daily, said that this was incredibly good thinking and highly recommended this to prevent attackers easy entry, and buy time for those in the room who cannot or do not want to carry for a variety of reasons and to allow time for first responders to react to the threat. Though Shane’s target wasn’t the Blackstone office, there was no way to know that at the time. Interesting either way. 

 “Blackstone employees barricaded their office in mere minutes.”
 

 Former CISA director Jen Easterly has become the latest target of Laura Loomer and the Trump administration, resulting in the Army rescinding her role at West Point. Driven by political pressure, it shows ongoing tensions between cybersecurity experts from the Biden-era CISA and current political feelings around censorship regarding political interference, COVID, and other areas. I personally have no horse in this race, but I do think CISA made a number of questionable moves during the COVID and 2020 election cycle, lost a lot of trust, and is perceived as being quite partisan. 

 “Former CISA director Jen Easterly”
 

 The American company Raytheon has secured a large contract for the production of AIM-120 AMRAAM missiles, with foreign customers including Ukraine. One of the interesting thing about these missiles is that while they were primarily designed for air-to-air missions, they have proven to be quite effective as surface to air missiles. 

 “AIM-120 AMRAAM”
 

 The Pentagon has scheduled its first major test of the Golden Dome missile defense system for just before the 2028 election . The Missile Defense Agency is planning to call the test FTI-X, indicating that it will involve the system's many sensors and weapons systems working together to engage multiple targets. This makes things like mutually assured destruction a lot less viable for those who don’t have these types of systems. The US got a lot of flak for its Star Wars program back in the 80s, but ultimately it didn’t lead to escalation, and I think this is likely a similar situation, and could limit errant balloons and other high-flying reconnaissance systems from entering US airspace. 

 In Tech news , the Tea app data breach has escalated, with the stolen data now being shared on hacking forums and a second database discovered containing 1.1 million private messages exchanged between the app's members. We now have a very real path for people to sue the users for defamation and hold them liable. Yet another case for ephemeral messaging. 

 China's cyberspace regulator has called Nvidia over alleged "serious security issues" in H20 AI chips aimed at the Chinese market . The regulator has raised concerns about location-tracking and remote shut-down capabilities, demanding detailed explanations about the alleged backdoor. I am not sure if this is real or not, but it would explain why the US had a change of heart about shipping them to the Chinese market. If they can be found to be monitored, destroyed using kinetic options, or disabled remotely, that makes them much less of a threat. 

 In Economic news , margin debt has reached a historic high of $1.008 trillion , surpassing levels seen at the peak of the dot-com bubble and the 2008 crash. This unprecedented level of leverage in the markets isn’t a great signal, indicating heightened risk and potential vulnerability to market downturns. Pretty bad signal for investors if they can’t find a way to pay it back with higher stocks. 

 “Margin debt just hit $1.008 trillion.”
 

 Okay, onto the articles! 

 Geopolitics 

 Russia has deployed its hypersonic missile, Oreshnik, in Belarus and plans to deploy it in other countries, including Europe, due to the possibility of NATO allies using longer-range missiles against Russia. 

 Russia has already used the Oreshnik missile against Ukraine in November 2025, and its capabilities include multiple warheads that can be immune to interception and have a devastating impact. 

 The deployment of Oreshnik missiles could extend Russia's influence in Europe and potentially create new security threats for NATO allies. 

 [RSnake: The lack of accuracy makes it more of a terror weapon akin to the V2 rocket used by Germany in WWII than a real strategic threat.] 

Source: https://www.military.com/daily-news/2025/08/01/putin-says-russias-hypersonic-missile-has-entered-service-and-will-be-deployed-belarus.html 

 

 The U.S. has imposed significant tariff increases on a wide range of goods from multiple trading partners, resulting in a sharp decline in global stock markets and heightened economic uncertainty. Countries such as Switzerland and India are seeking negotiations to mitigate the impact of these tariffs, while the U.S. itself has seen a slowdown in job growth and is facing internal and external pressures regarding trade policies. 

 The U.S. is implementing steep tariffs on imports from many countries, driving global markets down. 

 Countries affected by the tariffs are seeking negotiations to lower the rates and mitigate economic damage. 

 [RSnake: Around 100k jobs were lost due to DOGE, which weren’t good jobs in the sense that they were a drag on the economy. That said, AI is hurting tech employment, which will hurt job numbers, even if the rest of the economy is doing relatively fine.] 

Source: https://gcaptain.com/?p=232222 

 

 The Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB) is shutting down due to nearly $1.1 billion in funding cuts resulting from recent legislative actions. This marks a significant reduction in federal support for public media, impacting organizations like NPR and PBS that serve millions of Americans. 

 The CPB announced an orderly wind-down of its operations in response to severe funding cuts. 

 Legislation passed by Congress reflects a long-standing priority among Republicans to defund public media. 

 [RSnake: Once upon a time, before the Internet, it really did make a lot of sense to have a public broadcast. Now, there is extremely limited utility because access to information is both inexpensive and extremely pervasive. There are very few areas that this will affect so negatively as to limit education for the vast majority of Americans.] 

Source: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/1/corporation-for-public-broadcasting-to-shutter-following-trump-era-cuts?traffic_source=rss 

 

 Britain's Prime Minister Keir Starmer plans to recognize a Palestinian state at the UN General Assembly, aiming to revive the stalled two-state solution amid ongoing Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank. The Israeli government continues to pursue extensive settlement projects, deemed illegal by international law, while tensions rise as violent incidents involving settlers increase against Palestinian communities. The situation reflects historical grievances and ongoing conflicts over land and sovereignty in the region. 

 Keir Starmer intends to recognize a Palestinian state at the UN, seeking to re-establish the two-state solution. 

 Israeli settlement expansion in the West Bank persists, leading to increased violence against Palestinian communities. 

 [RSnake: It’s very clear that the UK is becoming more comfortable aligning with Muslim extremist groups. Why, though, I would have to defer to an expert on that, but it doesn’t seem they are taking their own population changes due to immigration from the Middle East and increases in immigration censorship seriously.] 

Source: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd6n0eeqp54o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss 

 

 Nigeria has rejected U.S. demands to accept third-country migrants as part of a broader immigration policy, asserting its sovereignty and prioritizing domestic challenges. This decision marks a significant shift in U.S.-Africa relations and may impact future cooperation between Nigeria and the United States amidst ongoing geopolitical dynamics. The refusal signifies a potential turning point for many African nations questioning their alignment with Western policies. 

 Nigeria has firmly declined U.S. requests to accept deported migrants, emphasizing its own domestic issues. 

 The decision may reshape Nigeria's diplomatic relationships and assert its independence on the global stage. 

 [RSnake: We don’t have a great relationship with Nigeria. Keep in mind that one of the largest means of income to Nigeria is the 419 Advance Fee scam . Speaking of Nigeria…] 

Source: https://foreignpolicy.com/?p=1202330 

 

 In Zamfara state, Nigeria, bandits killed at least 38 hostages despite ransom payments. The incident reflects the ongoing crisis of kidnapping for ransom by criminal gangs in the region, which has seen families feeling pressured to pay for the safety of their loved ones amidst government failures to ensure security. 

 Kidnapping in Nigeria continues to escalate with criminal gangs known as bandits targeting local populations for ransom. 

 Despite recent laws aimed at curbing ransom payments, families often feel compelled to pay to secure the release of their loved ones. 

 [RSnake: This is not a modern country with the same kinds of law enforcement that we have in the United States. Kidnapping and ransom is on the rise. Make sure you have K&R insurance if you travel there.] 

Source: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm2vyw9prlzo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss 

 

 The United States is preparing for a nuclear conflict with Russia following threats made by a former Russian president. President Donald Trump has authorized the deployment of nuclear submarines to ensure the safety of US citizens in light of these threats. Tensions between the US and Russia are escalating, with diplomatic exchanges indicating a potential for military confrontation. 

 US President Donald Trump ordered the deployment of nuclear submarines after threats from a former Russian leader. 

 Escalating tensions between the US and Russia could lead to military confrontation due to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine. 

 [RSnake: In a real comedic moment, the Russians asked exactly where the subs would be positioned. They were met with silence. Guess it doesn’t hurt to ask. 🤡 ] 

Source: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/2/7524490/ 

 

 The U.S. has implemented its largest sanctions crackdown on Iran since 2018, targeting a sophisticated shipping network involved in transporting Iranian and Russian oil while evading international sanctions. The sanctions package includes over 50 individuals and entities, as well as numerous vessels linked to an operation that allegedly supports the Iranian regime's activities and military logistics through complex evasion tactics. 

 The U.S. Department of the Treasury has designated over 50 individuals and entities connected to an Iranian shipping empire. 

 The crackdown aims to disrupt sophisticated methods used to transport and profit from sanctioned Iranian and Russian petroleum products. 

 [RSnake: This will hurt Russia and Iran both. The more we can make their relationship hurt, the better it is for us and Ukraine.] 

Source: https://gcaptain.com/?p=232101 

 

 A powerful 8.8 magnitude earthquake off the Russian coast caused tsunami waves to flood the coastal town of Severo-Kurilsk. The earthquake is noted as the largest to occur globally since 2011, prompting alerts for potential further impacts from aftershocks or tsunami activity. 

 An 8.8 magnitude earthquake occurred near the Russian coast. 

 Tsunami waves flooded the town of Severo-Kurilsk due to the earthquake. 

 [RSnake: That is a pretty crazy earthquake and it set off a series of smaller tremors all over the pacific rim.] 

Source: https://abcnews.go.com/International/video/tsunami-waves-swamp-russian-coastal-town-124201639 

 

 The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has revoked the 2009 endangerment finding for greenhouse gas emissions, stating that it no longer has the authority to regulate these gases under the Clean Air Act. This decision is anticipated to have significant economic implications, potentially saving the American economy billions in regulatory costs and changing the approach to climate policy. 

 The EPA's revocation of the endangerment finding could free the American economy from costly greenhouse gas regulations. 

 The administration argues that carbon dioxide does not pose a significant danger to public health, thereby challenging existing climate policies. 

 [RSnake: This really mostly affects CO2 emissions, which means carbon credits are not a thing people have to worry about anymore in the US, unless they have some other reason to need it, like publicity around cutting carbon emissions, etc.] 

Source: https://www.dailywire.com/news/winning-trumps-epa-wrecks-the-radical-green-agenda 

 

 Greece has suspended the right to seek asylum for new migrants for at least three months due to a significant increase in crossings from Libya, citing a state of emergency. Migrants, including those fleeing war in Sudan, are being detained and transferred to closed facilities, prompting criticism from human rights advocates regarding the legality and humanitarian implications of the government's actions. 

 Greece has moved to detain migrants arriving illegally and suspended their right to apply for asylum. 

 The situation at the border reflects broader trends in European migration policies amid increasing arrivals. 

 [RSnake: I have a feeling Europe is at a tipping point and will need to make some hard decisions about whether it wants to keep its culture, languages, and traditions or if it wants Sharia law. The two won’t coexist peacefully.] 

Source: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgp5rexnk2o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss 

 

 Kansas Attorney General Kris Kobach has requested an investigation from the Justice Department into Energy Foundation China, alleging that the organization, linked to the Chinese Communist Party, is engaging in practices that are detrimental to American energy production. The request follows claims that the organization is funding litigation to hinder American industry while promoting dependence on foreign technology in climate initiatives. 

 The Kansas AG's letter emphasizes the strategic disadvantage posed by foreign influence on American energy policies. 

 The issue involves accusations of climate-related lawfare being used to undermine U.S. energy independence. 

 [RSnake: It’ll be interesting to see how state AGs wage war on China through state power. This is just one example. The other being seizing assets based on COVID misinformation/lab leaks from China.] 

Source: https://www.dailywire.com/news/climate-lawfare-kansas-ag-asks-justice-department-to-investigate-chinese-climate-firm 

 Cybersecurity 

 Apple has released iOS 18.6, introducing over 20 security patches, including one addressing a critical vulnerability in open-source code that has already been exploited against Chrome users. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has mandated that federal agencies update their software by August 12 due to the severity of this flaw, which could allow unauthorized code execution on various Apple operating systems. 

 iOS 18.6 includes crucial security patches, with one vulnerability impacting open-source code exploited in Chrome. 

 CISA is requiring federal agencies to address this vulnerability by updating their software by a specific deadline. 

 [RSnake: And so should you, if you haven’t already. Keep in mind Blackhat is coming this week, so a lot of new exploits will be traded by hackers this week, so better safe than sorry.] 

Source: https://lifehacker.com/tech/apple-security-patch-fixes-chrome-vulnerability?utm_medium=RSS 

 

 A significant amount of personally identifiable information (PII) has been discovered in the DataComp CommonPool data set, which is widely used for training image generation models. This includes images of sensitive documents and data from individuals, raising serious privacy concerns as the dataset contains hundreds of millions of potentially identifiable images due to extensive web scraping practices. 

 Millions of images containing sensitive, personally identifiable information were found in a major AI training dataset. 

 The dataset's creation involved web scraping, raising significant privacy and data protection issues. 

 [RSnake: Yep, this one will end up on aiidoinggreat.com . 😆 ] 

Source: https://www.technologyreview.com/2025/07/18/1120466/a-major-ai-training-data-set-contains-millions-of-examples-of-personal-data/ 

 

 In Russia, major cyberattacks are causing widespread disruptions in various sectors, including retail and aviation. Notable incidents include outages at the Vkusvill supermarket chain and the Samokat delivery app, along with a significant attack on Aeroflot that resulted in the loss of 250 million rubles and the cancellation of over 100 flights. 

 Vkusvill and Samokat faced simultaneous technical disruptions due to cyberattacks. 

 Aeroflot suffered a major cyberattack that halted operations and led to significant financial losses. 

 [RSnake: War is hell. But this is the kind of thing that starts impacting normal Russians who won’t be happy about this and will likely want the pain to stop. More on the Aeroflot compromise .] 

Source: https://euromaidanpress.com/?p=352435 

 

 A vulnerability in the Tea dating app exposed users' direct messages, leading the company to disable this feature. An independent security researcher reported that unauthorized access lasted until late last week, prompting Senator Ron Wyden to call for an investigation into the incident. 

 A security vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to users' direct messages. 

 Senator Ron Wyden is demanding an investigation into the incident. 

 [RSnake: I bet we find that no one competent was involved in the development of the app.] 

Source: https://www.404media.co/tea-app-turns-off-dms-after-exposing-messages-about-abortions-cheating/ 

 

 Iran is disconnecting users' phone SIM cards and forcing them to sign a pledge not to criticize the state on social media in order to regain access, with instructions requiring 20 posts of praise for the Islamic Republic. 

 Iran is using phone service cuts to silence dissent and requires users to post praise of the ruling system on social media to regain access. 

 The disconnection of SIM card services was implemented without prior warning or judicial order. 

 [RSnake: Good old authoritarian regimes… You can always trust them to hurt their population more than the enemy.] 

Source: https://www.iranintl.com/en/202507291928 

 

 A Federal Aviation Administration official revealed that an air traffic controller did not inform a commercial plane crew of an approaching Army helicopter prior to a mid-air collision in Washington, D.C., resulting in the deaths of 67 people. The incident has raised questions about the safety practices and staffing levels at the airport, where controllers expressed feeling overwhelmed by the high volume of air traffic. 

 The FAA stated that the air traffic controller failed to notify the plane crew of a converging helicopter, which led to a fatal crash. 

 NTSB hearings indicated staffing and communication issues as contributing factors to the tragedy. 

 [RSnake: This whole system feels like it needs a major overhaul and rethink, where computers do the bulk of the work or at least oversight.] 

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/us/air-traffic-controller-should-have-warned-plane-army-helicopters-path-ahead-fatal-dc-crash-faa 

 

 Security researchers have demonstrated exploits for critical vulnerabilities in Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE), allowing unauthenticated remote code execution and potentially leading to malicious activity. 

 Cisco has disclosed two severe vulnerabilities in its ISE software that allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges. 

 A security researcher has published a detailed write-up of the exploit chain for these vulnerabilities, providing technical details and payload structure necessary for skilled hackers to recreate the attack. 

 [RSnake: Attackers will attack what they can hit. For the most part, these are external devices, which happen to be security products. Cisco is one such company.] 

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/exploit-available-for-critical-cisco-ise-bug-exploited-in-attacks/ 

 

 A high-severity vulnerability in PaperCut NG/MF print management software has been exploited by threat actors, allowing them to gain remote code execution in cross-site request forgery (CSRF) attacks. CISA is warning organizations to patch their systems immediately due to the ongoing attacks. 

 CISA has issued a warning about the vulnerability and urged organizations to prioritize patching this actively exploited security bug as soon as possible. 

 The vulnerability was tracked as CVE-2023-2533 and can allow an attacker to alter security settings or execute arbitrary code if the target is an admin with a current login session. 

 [RSnake: It’s rare for CSRF to be exploited in the wild. Interesting.] 

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-flags-papercut-rce-bug-as-exploited-in-attacks-patch-now/ 

 

 Cybercrime is rising globally with a potential annual ransomware cost of $265 billion by 2031 and a total of $10.5 trillion this year, driven by AI-powered criminal activities. 

 The first quarter of 2025 saw a 126 percent surge in ransomware incidents, with high-impact attacks against high-profile brands and institutions. 

 Artificial intelligence has become a potent force multiplier for the criminal underground, enabling sophisticated attacks using generative models and cloud-hosted toolkits. 

 [RSnake: AI certainly helps, but the real explosion will be once AI learns how to create it’s own 0day autonomously. ] 

Source: https://cybersecurityventures.com/?p=33746 

 

 Over 250 fake mobile apps in Korea are spreading spyware, leading to personal data theft and extortion. These apps, which mimic popular services, have been tricking users into granting permissions that allow hackers to access sensitive personal information. 

 More than 250 malicious mobile apps in Korea have been identified, containing spyware. 

 Victims of these apps are experiencing data theft and subsequent blackmail by the attackers. 

 [RSnake: These are definitely a lot more prevalent than they used to be, especially on Android and 3rd party Android app stores.] 

Source: https://www.darkreading.com/threat-intelligence/koreans-hacked-blackmailed-250-fake-mobile-apps 

 Technology 

 A 17-year-old mathematician, Hannah Cairo, has recently disproven a 40-year-old mathematical conjecture known as the Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture, impacting the field of harmonic analysis. This achievement has surprised the mathematical community, as Cairo completed the proof while still in high school and is now poised to begin her doctoral studies without a prior college degree. 

 Hannah Cairo disproved the Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture, an important problem in harmonic analysis. 

 Her work challenges established beliefs in the field and encourages new research directions. 

 [RSnake: For the math nerds out there…] 

Source: https://www.quantamagazine.org/at-17-hannah-cairo-solved-a-major-math-mystery-20250801/ 

 

 A federal appeals court upheld a ruling that found Google’s Android app store to be an illegal monopoly, following a lawsuit by Epic Games. This decision may lead to significant changes in how the app store operates, potentially increasing competition and consumer options. Google is also facing additional legal challenges regarding its search engine and advertising practices, which may result in further regulatory changes. 

 Google's Android app store is now deemed an illegal monopoly, impacting its operations. 

 Epic Games successfully challenged Google's practices, prompting potential changes beneficial to competitors. 

 Google is confronting ongoing legal issues that may reshape its overall business structure. 

 [RSnake: I found them to be intolerable when we were deploying a new phone. You couldn’t deploy the OS with the app store without also having to use Chrome pinned to Google as the default search. So yeah, they absolutely are anti-competitive.] 

Source: https://www.fastcompany.com/91378959/google-loses-appeal-antitrust-epic-games 

 

 China's Unitree Robotics has unveiled a humanoid robot that can fist-fight and perform cartwheels, challenging Tesla's Optimus as the leading humanoid robot, with potential for 1 billion humanoids in use by 2050 and a $5 trillion industry. 

 Unitree Robotics is challenging Tesla's Optimus as the leading humanoid robot with its new humanoid robot that can fist-fight and perform cartwheels. 

 The global humanoid robotics market is projected to reach $5 trillion by 2050, with over 1 billion humanoids potentially in use by then. 

 [RSnake: Yep, they’ll challenge us, so we need to push harder to have higher quality, fewer backdoors, malware, and surveillance, etc. This is where tariffs might actually be extremely useful.] 

Source: https://www.zerohedge.com/technology/watch-china-robot-giant-unveils-tesla-optimus-killer-can-fist-fight 

 A proposed data center in Wyoming, USA is planned to consume more electricity than the entire state currently uses annually at full deployment. 

 The facility would start at 1.8 gigawatts and scale up to 10 gigawatts of power use, consuming nearly five times the electricity used by every household in the state combined. 

 At its full capacity, the proposed data center would consume 87.6 TWh of electricity annually, double the entire state currently generates. 

 [RSnake: More nuclear energy is needed and fast until Fusion is available.] 

Source: https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2025/07/ai-in-wyoming-may-soon-use-more-electricity-than-states-human-residents/ 

 Business 

 OpenAI has successfully raised $8.3 billion in a funding round, aiming to reach a total of $40 billion by the end of the year at a valuation of $300 billion. This funding round saw high demand, being five times oversubscribed, and established OpenAI as the leader in AI funding, significantly outpacing its competitors. 

 OpenAI raised $8.3 billion, part of its goal to reach $40 billion by year-end. 

 The funding round was oversubscribed, indicating high investor demand. 

 OpenAI's annual recurring revenue exceeded $13 billion and may surpass $20 billion by year’s end. 

 [RSnake: Pretty crazy, given they still haven’t shown a business model that would get them anywhere near those numbers, especially given their costs are way higher than their income.] 

Source: https://fortune.com/2025/08/01/openai-funding-oversubscribed-early-investors-new-partners-dragoneer/ 

 

 Oxide has raised $100M Series B funding, led by new existing Oxide investors, to build a large, durable, public company in the cloud computing on-premises market. 

 Oxide aims to build a huge market for cloud computing on-premises and is uniquely positioned to serve it. 

 The company will use the funding to address its customers' most pressing questions around scale and roadmap scope. 

 [RSnake: Good for them! I am personally fond of the I/ONX guys . If you’re interested in this space, check those guys out.] 

Source: https://oxide.computer/blog/our-100m-series-b 

 

 A $14.6 billion healthcare fraud scheme has been uncovered, with 300 defendants charged for misleading patients into paying for unnecessary medical care. 

 Candace Taylor, a Louisiana woman, allegedly purchased a Lamborghini while receiving Medicaid benefits and is facing a fraud charge. 

 The scheme involved transferring tens of thousands of dollars between personal and business accounts to qualify for Medicaid benefits. 

 [RSnake: If you know people on AARP, this is a good one to send to them, to make sure their next bill is real.] 

Source: https://www.foxnews.com/us/louisiana-medicaid-millionaire-lamborghini-claiming-government-benefits-years 

 

 The U.S. jobs report indicates significantly lower job growth than anticipated, with only 73,000 jobs added in July and downward revisions of previous months revealing a much weaker labor market. This has led to expectations that the Federal Reserve may implement rate cuts sooner, as the unemployment rate also increased to 4.2%. Concerns are rising about the impact of ongoing trade tensions and tariffs on job creation in various sectors. 

 U.S. job growth has stalled unexpectedly with a significant drop in previous payroll figures. 

 Expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts are increasing in response to the weak jobs report and rising unemployment rates. 

 [RSnake: Yup, not pretty, and Trump is not happy with that team that analyzes these numbers. But ultimately we just don’t have a lot of new job options, and the highest end of the market is using AI to remove jobs, not add them.] 

Source: https://fortune.com/2025/08/01/jobs-report-july-downward-revisions-fed-rate-cuts-jerome-powell/ 

 

 Figma has successfully completed its IPO with a share price of $98, significantly exceeding initial projections and achieving a valuation of $19.3 billion. The company has shifted its focus from just professional designers to appealing to a broader user base, reflecting an expansion in product offerings and overall demand in the software market. 

 Figma's IPO achieved a valuation of $19.3 billion. 

 The company aims to target a wider audience beyond just professional designers. 

 [RSnake: Good for them. It’s a good product and quite useful for lots of teams.] 

Source: https://www.fastcompany.com/91377945/figma-ipo-why-figmas-future-success-doesnt-rely-on-designers 

 

 The U.S. trucking industry is currently experiencing a significant labor shortage, exacerbated by the Trump administration's directive to enforce English proficiency requirements for truck drivers. Approximately 140,000 drivers could potentially be sidelined due to these new regulations at a time when the industry already faces a shortage of over 82,000 drivers, a number expected to exceed 160,000 by 2030. 

 The Trump administration's updated English language proficiency requirements may remove thousands of drivers from the U.S. trucking workforce. 

 The trucking industry is grappling with an acute labor shortage, which could worsen due to new hiring obstacles stemming from language requirements. 

 [RSnake: Makes sense. On the other hand, I bet English teachers specializing in trucking would make a killing right about now.] 

Source: https://www.supplychainbrain.com/articles/42209-new-english-language-rules-for-truckers-threaten-to-deepen-staffing-crisis 

 Share this newsletter 

 Got a useful tip? Looking to chat with me? Click here . 

 Check out the RSnake Show as well. 

 Full Disclosure: None of this is advice. This newsletter is strictly educational and my opinions. Please be careful, do your own research, and consult a professional before taking action on anything posited here.

subject: RSnake Report 20250727
subtitle: Cambodia vs Thailand, MLK files release, etc
body_text:
What's In the News

 Geopols 

 Cybersecurity 

 Technology 

 Business 

 Hello, and thanks for reading! Been a really nice, warm summer so far. We’ll have a big announcement coming this coming week, but for now, we’re just getting ready for Blackhat. For those who are unaware I am on the CISO advisory board, but also on the Innovator and Investor summit board, and the Cyber Insurance Summit board. Busy times! 

 In Russia/Ukraine news , Ukrainian forces have been relentlessly launching kamikaze drone attacks on Russian territory , including Moscow. This tactic serves multiple purposes: it aims to overload Russian air defense systems, expose vulnerabilities, and establish safe corridors for future major strikes. Said another way, the Ukrainians are mapping out the battlefield and pinpointing the most effective missile routes, setting the stage for an escalation. 

 Russia, for its part, is gearing up for a massive offensive, amassing a stockpile of 160,000 drones . For context, the Russians are planning to launch something like 78k drones in 2025, so this is double the stockpile. Russia is preparing to launch a massive drone attack on Ukraine, with plans to send up to 2,000 drones in a single night . Ukraine's need for additional low-cost air defense systems is now becoming increasingly apparent. Either way, this points towards a new big offensive on both sides that has not started yet. 

 “160,000 drones”
 

 Ukrainian drones have struck a railway station in Novocherkassk , located in Russia's Rostov region. In recent days, Ukraine has hit a thermal power plant supplying electricity to southern Russian railways, a railway bridge , and now a southern Russian railway marshaling yard. It makes a lot of sense given how dependent the Russians are to rail for commerce and their military. 

 Ukrainian drones have targeted the Signal defense plant in Stavropol , a critical facility within Russia's military-industrial complex. The plant is responsible for producing radio-electronic equipment used in combat aircraft, air defense systems, and electronic warfare systems . 

 “Radio equipment factory 'Signal' in Stavropol”
 

 A Russian oil depot in Adler came under a drone attack . As we saw a lot in 2024, the Russian economy depends heavily on oil, but it is generally rebuilding fairly quickly, so the Ukrainians have to keep pressure on various different oil transport and oil storage facilities if they want to keep the economic stress on the Kremlin. 

 “oil depot in Adler”
 

 Germany has committed to providing Ukraine with five Patriot air defense systems. This should greatly reduce the likelihood of volleys of drones making their way through. However, this doesn’t have a limitless supply of missiles, so it’s safe to say that saturation drone attacks will likely still have effect on target, no matter how good these systems are. Each Patriot battery typically consists of a command post, radar, six to eight launchers, and support vehicles. 

 “five much-needed Patriot systems”
 

 An interesting post I saw was from secretsqrl123 : To paraphrase, Russia initially invaded Ukraine with approximately 700k troops, later bolstered by 300k conscripts, 100k+ volunteers from various regions, 200k from the Russian Guard, 300k from Storm Z, 100k from private military companies, 30k from North Korea, and 20k from overseas. With an additional 30k+ troops added monthly, Russia's total force approaches three million by those numbers. However, it is estimated that only 700k to 800k troops are currently on the front lines, leaving the whereabouts of the remaining two million troops a mystery. Naysayers will say it’s more like one million missing troops, and that is accounted for in the loss data.
